status: candidate, unreleased; prepared from a complete local benchmark record
release_status: not an official 0.2.1 or 0.2.2 release; candidate for 0.2.2 review

environment.memory_observation_scope: Linux cgroup v2 memory.max, not physical host memory

native_release_probe.scope: default release compiler regression; same current full runtime; no auto/core throughput claim
native_release_probe.conditions: same source/runtime paths and seed lock; ordinary release profile; jobs2; warm registry/OS caches; shared Cargo target; alternating native execution order
native_release_probe.interpretation: Native execution only. Build measurements used a shared target in fixed order and are not presented as a before/after build comparison.

known_version_database_audit.limits: Known-version matches in this frozen database only; not proof of vulnerability absence or exploit validation

limitations: Offline and warm-cache only; no network/index/download performance measured.
Does not measure CI behavior, whole-backend throughput, or native application throughput.
Dependency graph versions differ between paths; the data cannot isolate lock-seeding algorithm causality or establish a general speed ratio.
Seed lock is opt-in/default-off and is a reproducibility feature; clean full builds regress in this sample.
Fresh/compiled artifact counts on newapp are the same within each path between ordinary and seed; this is not evidence of a cache-hit improvement.
A prior interrupted P2 trial was excluded; see README for the separately scoped FIFO refusal observation.
The known-version audit used one frozen RustSec database commit; zero matches in that database is not proof of vulnerability absence or exploit safety.
RSS is a one-child high-water measurement and can reflect launcher/fork/exec behavior; it is not steady-state Rust heap usage or a whole-process-tree/cgroup peak.
